title: Cloudflare doubles long-context capacity for Kimi while cutting GLM memory use
friendlyTitle: Cloudflare fits more AI work onto the same hardware
summary: Cloudflare detailed production techniques for serving large open models: an 8-bit KV cache doubled Kimi K2.6 context capacity, while 4-bit weight compression cut GLM 5.2’s checkpoint size by about 40%. Its evaluations found no meaningful accuracy loss in the tested workloads.
friendlySummary: Cloudflare made Kimi and GLM models use much less GPU memory while keeping similar test results.
whyItMatters: Inference engineering can reduce AI cost and latency without waiting for a new model. Teams running open models can use the same ideas—careful quantization, benchmarking and cache isolation—to serve more users on existing hardware.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Better efficiency can mean faster and cheaper AI services without buying as many expensive GPUs.
